papers.title: The Wild West of Nomenclature, Definitions, and Methodologies in Rodent Sleep Scoring.
papers.summary: This perspective examines variability in rodent sleep-scoring nomenclature, definitions, and methodologies, illustrating how choices such as epoch duration and bout criteria alter sleep-stage assignment and apparent fragmentation/consolidation. It proposes consistent terminology, explicit operational definitions, and minimum reporting practices to improve reproducibility and cross-study comparison.

papers.title: MM-SleepNet: An Automatic Sleep Staging Network Based on Modal Re-Weighting and Mamba.
papers.summary: The paper proposes MM-SleepNet, an automatic sleep staging network using modal re-weighting and a bidirectional Mamba encoder to learn contextual information across epochs. On Sleep-EDF and ISRUC datasets, MM-SleepNet outperformed state-of-the-art methods, and ablation experiments demonstrated the effectiveness of its modules.

papers.title: Repeated self-administered EEG recordings enable longitudinal measurement of brain activity at home
papers.summary: Five participants completed repeated self-administered four-channel consumer EEG recordings at home during rest and an auditory oddball task with and without cognitive load, capturing alpha increases with eye closure, load-related theta changes, and clear event-related responses. Aggregating sessions improved reliability, with split-half reliability of the N1-like response rising from r = .22 for one session to r = .76 for seven sessions per half.

papers.title: EEG-Based Recognition of Self-Imagined Emotions Using Multi-Domain Features and Subject-Specific Calibration.
papers.summary: The study evaluated a multi-domain EEG decoding framework for self-imagined emotion recognition using time-frequency features, functional and effective connectivity, and subject-specific calibration in 38 participants. PLV-based features with SVM achieved 97.0% accuracy under pooled cross-validation but only ~25–30% under leave-one-subject-out, while subject-specific calibration using 75% of target data restored accuracy to 95.0%.

papers.title: Hemodynamic spectral signatures across vigilance states: a whole-night EEG/fNIRS investigation.
papers.summary: Using whole-night EEG and fNIRS in healthy young adults, the study characterized cortical hemodynamic spectral signatures across vigilance states, showing slow-frequency (0.002–0.1 Hz) power increased in N1 and attenuated across N2/N3, while very-low-frequency (<0.01 Hz) power re-emerged in REM. Higher-frequency oscillations (0.15–0.5 Hz) were enhanced during NREM sleep and returned toward wake-like levels in REM.

papers.title: Simulation-based neural dynamics of stress-related negative cognitive bias in depressive symptoms: a dynamical EEG/ERP framework.
papers.summary: Developed a simulation-based nonlinear state-space framework with three states (negative bias, cognitive control, arousal) linking stress-related negative cognitive bias to EEG/ERP measures, testing it on 180 simulated participants. The pre-specified quartic model achieved mean held-out RMSE 0.060 versus 0.436 for an interaction-only candidate, and state-reconstruction RMSE rose from 0.152 to 0.232 under 15% loading perturbations; these are model-sensitivity results, not clinical effect estimates.

papers.title: Theoretical analysis of transfer learning for temporally dependent observations.
papers.journal: Bernoulli : official journal of the Bernoulli Society for Mathematical Statistics and Probability
papers.summary: Proposed a two-step transfer learning procedure for high-dimensional vector autoregressive models with temporally dependent observations, including auxiliary-set selection and debiasing techniques for parameter inference and confidence intervals. Under mild conditions allowing heavy tails and dependence, the method attains the minimax rate, with empirical validation on simulated data and an EEG dataset.

papers.title: A Lightweight Hybrid-Attention Conformer for Affective State Recognition from Wearable EEG.
papers.summary: The paper introduces KimiFormer, a lightweight hybrid-attention Conformer that classifies raw wearable EEG for affective state recognition, using a spatio-temporal stemming module and stacked Conformer blocks with linear/full attention. It achieved 95.5% accuracy on the EEG Violence Dataset but near-chance subject-independent performance on DREAMER (balanced accuracy 52.7% valence, 50.2% arousal), with 3.2M parameters and 15.64 ms inference latency.

papers.title: EEG Biomarkers for Stress Detection: A Comparative Analysis of Hjorth Parameters, Spectral and Fractal-Dimension Measures.
papers.summary: Compared Hjorth parameters, fractal-dimension measures, and conventional spectral band-power features for EEG-based stress detection using ANOVA-based feature selection and multiple machine-learning classifiers on pre-recorded stress-experiment data. Hjorth activity, frontal β asymmetry, and the γ/θ ratio were among the most frequently selected features, and combined feature spaces including Hjorth parameters and fractal dimensions outperformed the conventional spectral-feature reference configuration.

papers.title: Sequential syntax of EEG microstates captures the temporal dynamics of inhibitory control.
papers.summary: Applied a sequence-based framework combining conditional successor analysis with multiple sequence alignment to EEG microstate sequences from 30 healthy adults during a Go/NoGo task. Conditional successor analysis identified three NoGo-early motifs (A-C-D, B-A-D, E-A-D) passing through microstate A and ending in D, while sequence alignment showed non-random temporal organization across all conditions.

papers.title: Automatic classification of seizure adequacy in electroconvulsive therapy: A proof-of-concept study
papers.summary: Using 1000 ECT session EEGs from 130 patients labeled by experts into null-response, threshold, and adequate seizure quality categories, the authors trained machine learning classifiers on raw EEG and achieved AUC >0.9 for 0 vs. threshold and threshold vs. adequate discrimination, though prediction of seizure quality in subsequent treatments was only moderate. Adding clinical variables did not improve performance.

papers.title: Effects of Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring During Polysomnography on Sleep Indices and EEG Power.
papers.summary: Secondary analysis of a balanced two-night crossover in 72 healthy adults assessing how ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) and first-night effect alter polysomnographic sleep indices and EEG power. Both ABPM and first-night effect were associated with lower composite sleep quality index, ABPM with higher light-sleep and lower N3 percentages and higher relative theta power, and 60.3% of in-sleep ABPM measurements contained at least one arousal detection within the 2-min window.

papers.title: Distinct contemplative traditions share a common EEG complexity signature
papers.summary: Used EEG from 226 participants (advanced meditators of four contemplative traditions and non-meditating controls) with a 21-feature neurodynamic profiling approach and machine learning to identify shared and tradition-specific signatures. Meditation was reliably separable from task states via a large uniform drop in complexity, while meditators differed from controls mainly in timescale dynamics, and a classifier trained on three traditions detected meditation in the held-out fourth, relying mainly on complexity features.

papers.title: Reproducible EEG-BCI Experiments: Frame-Confirmed Timing and Physical SSVEP Validation.
papers.summary: Presented and evaluated an auditable EEG-BCI experimental workflow integrating machine-readable SSVEP protocols, deterministic session planning, frame-confirmed events, acquisition provenance, integrity checks, and photoresistor-based display validation. All 61 automated tests passed; 48 of 48 optical sweep measurements (8-15 Hz) fell within ±0.25 Hz (mean absolute error 0.0345 Hz, max 0.0668 Hz), though local optical pulse-width anomalies were observed at 13-14 Hz and in two multi-stimulus repetitions.

papers.title: Self-Organized Explainable Symbolic EEG Feature Engineering Using Directed Lobish and Previous-Next Pattern: A Proof-of-Concept Study on Dementia Classification.
papers.summary: Designed an interpretable symbolic EEG feature-engineering framework (SOXFE) combining Bipartite Channel Transformer, Previous-Next Pattern, cumulative-weight INCA selection, Directed Lobish explainability, and ensemble tkNN with combinational majority voting for dementia classification. Segment-wise 10-fold cross-validation reached 99.12-99.74% accuracy, but participant-independent accuracy fell to 51.19-63.81% (LOSO) and 49.00-62.50% (nested participant-grouped), with no McNemar advantage over majority-class baselines, so clinical diagnostic utility was not established.

papers.title: BioTWavePat: An EEG-Based Mental Performance Detection Model.
papers.summary: Introduced BioTWavePat-XFE, an EEG mental performance detection model using signed cross-rhythm channel-rank transition features, cumulative-weighted selectors, and Directed Lobish decoding, evaluated under three data-dependent selection protocols with participant-wise LOSO validation. Under leakage-restricted Protocol C, accuracies fell to 80.46% (STEW), 82.50% (TMPD), and 74.65% (MAT), showing whole-dataset selection inflated original estimates, with MAT near majority-prediction performance.

papers.title: EEG-based Deep Learning Reveals Cortical Sensitivity to Small Changes in Deep Brain Stimulation Parameters.
papers.summary: Recorded in-clinic EEG from Parkinson's disease patients during DBS programming and trained per-patient siamese EEGNet models to classify whether 1-second EEG segments came from the same or different DBS parameter settings, achieving average 74% accuracy. Ablation and explainability analyses identified mid-gamma (55-90 Hz) oscillations as the key discriminating band, independent of 1:2 gamma entrainment, indicating cortical sensitivity to small DBS parameter changes.

papers.title: EEG and hedonic responses to sonic-seasoning soundscapes: a dataset.
papers.summary: Releases an open dataset of 14-channel EMOTIV EPOC X EEG (128 Hz) from 30 adults exposed to two contrasting soundscapes, with synchronized event markers, resting calibration, per-soundscape liking ratings, stimulus audio files, and demographics. The data add a neurophysiological measurement angle to sonic-seasoning and multisensory marketing research, released as recorded with contact- and signal-quality indices retained for re-users.

papers.title: Automated Detection of Abnormal Pediatric Electroencephalograms Using Machine Learning: Retrospective Study.
papers.summary: Retrospectively compared a gradient boosting model with CNN-based deep learning models for automated detection of abnormal pediatric EEGs at a single university hospital. The DL model achieved higher sensitivity (78.3%) and F1-score (80%) while gradient boosting achieved higher specificity (93% vs 89.6%), with overall accuracies up to 85.3%.

papers.title: Temporal evolution of EEG band power at freezing of gait onset in Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: Analyzed EEG spectral power in 10 Parkinson's disease patients across 204 freezing-of-gait episodes during ecological walking using channel-wise piecewise linear mixed-effects models. Alpha power increased progressively pre-FoG at frontal and midline channels, while theta power increased abruptly at FoG onset at F3 and Fz, with no significant beta modulation after FDR correction.

papers.title: The Case for Low-Friction High-Adherence Passive Sleep-Tracking Devices in Longitudinal Monitoring of Neurodegenerative Disease.
papers.summary: Presents a perspective arguing that low-friction, high-adherence passive sleep-tracking devices such as smart rings, despite lower accuracy than EEG/PSG gold standards, may be preferable for longitudinal monitoring of neurodegenerative disease. Argues that long-term statistical benefits from detecting within-person changes and higher sampling frequency can offset accuracy trade-offs, with focus on Parkinson's disease sleep monitoring.

papers.title: Predicting Motor Recovery in the Subacute Phase of Stroke: The Role of Passive Motor Task and Electroencephalogram Brain Networks.
papers.summary: Compared passive robotic movement, active execution, motor imagery, and No-Go tasks as EEG-based prognostic predictors in 10 subacute stroke patients across two time points; the passive task model gave the strongest internal prediction (RMSE 5.94, nested LOSO CV-R2 0.91). Consistent prognostic features were ipsilesional/contralesional motor-area event-related desynchronization, characteristic path length, and clustering coefficient, with less overactivation and hyperconnectivity in the early subacute phase.

papers.title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model (CNN-GRU) with MRMR for EEG-Based Depression Detection.
papers.summary: Proposed a hybrid CNN-GRU deep learning framework with mRMR feature selection for EEG-based depression detection, evaluated on the MODMA dataset. Across 30 simulation runs, it achieved a mean classification accuracy of 96.74%, outperforming the comparison methods.

papers.title: Combined MEG and EEG suggest a limbic source network for the P3.
papers.summary: Re-evaluated P3 sources using combined MEG and EEG with MRI-based noise-normalized minimum-norm source analysis whose cortical source space included the hippocampal cornu ammonis. At the P3 peak, source analysis showed strong retrosplenial cortex and weaker hippocampal sources, with later insula and anterior mid-cingulate activity, supporting a limbic-system interpretation of the P3; simulations indicated combined MEG/EEG improved source specificity.

papers.title: Explainable Rhythm-Resolved EEG for Retrospective Comparison of Psychiatric-Service Adults with Recorded Violent Offences and Non-Clinical Controls.
papers.summary: Applied rhythm-resolved rank-transition EEG features (RhythmFluxPat) with an explainable classifier to retrospectively separate psychiatric-service adults with recorded violent offences from non-clinical controls. A nested tkNN classified 93/95 participants (97.89%), with DRLobish linking features to delta and beta-to-gamma versus theta and alpha-to-theta rhythm routes, while the authors caution these are optimistic internal estimates.

papers.title: Quantum-Kernel Learning for Subject-Independent EEG Emotion Recognition with Spectral-Connectivity Features.
papers.summary: Investigated state-fidelity-based quantum-kernel SVM learning for subject-independent EEG valence and arousal recognition using differential entropy and phase-locking value features from the DEAP dataset. Quantum-kernel SVM reached the highest mean balanced accuracy of 59.18% for valence, while Linear SVM with DE features led arousal at 54.16%, with comparable overall performance across classifiers.

papers.title: Cortical Network Alterations and Treatment-Induced Reorganization in Panic Disorder: A Longitudinal High-Density EEG Study.
papers.summary: In a longitudinal high-density EEG study, drug-naïve panic disorder patients showed frequency-specific cortical network disruptions (enhanced α-band connectivity within/between default mode, frontoparietal, and dorsal attention networks; reduced θ/δ connectivity) with 86.32% SVM classification accuracy versus controls, and these network features reorganized after 6 weeks of venlafaxine treatment alongside clinical improvement.

papers.title: Correlation and Agreement Between Bispectral Index Monitoring and Quantitative EEG in Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
papers.summary: Prospectively compared bispectral index (BIS) parameters with quantitative EEG in 64 aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage patients across 248 paired observations. BIS-tpw and BIS-sef showed moderate-to-strong correlations and fair-to-good agreement with qEEG power and spectral edge frequency, whereas BIS-v showed weak correlations and poor agreement.

papers.title: Electrophysiology of multisite direct electrical stimulation in the human brain
papers.summary: Using stereo-EEG in 20 participants, this study characterized electrophysiological responses to simultaneous multisite direct electrical stimulation, finding that dual-site stimulation engaged larger networks than single-site, responses were mostly explained by linear superposition but included sublinear (proximal) and supralinear (network-connected late) nonlinearities, and low-intensity dual-site stimulation matched or exceeded higher-intensity single-site stimulation.

papers.title: Interpersonal alignment in infra-slow EEG rhythms and bodily signals anticipates mutual recognition
papers.summary: Recorded infra-slow EEG alongside respiratory, cardiac and skin conductance signals during the perceptual crossing hyperscanning paradigm, contrasting dyads that achieved mutual recognition with those that did not. Mutual recognition trials showed enhanced inter-participant alignment of 0.1 Hz infra-slow EEG power and differences in respiratory depth, cardiac vagal index and skin conductance, suggesting infra-slow rhythms as a temporal scaffold for interpersonal brain-body coordination.

papers.title: Brain-computer interfaces for neurodegenerative diseases: A comprehensive review of closed-loop systems from diagnosis to neural rehabilitation.
papers.summary: This comprehensive review analyzes brain-computer interface (BCI) development and closed-loop systems for neurodegenerative diseases, focusing on applications in Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis for early diagnosis, functional reconstruction, and neuromodulation, and discusses technical, clinical translation, and ethical challenges plus future directions such as multimodal fusion and adaptive algorithms.

papers.title: Investigation of Brain Performance in the Schizophrenia Spectrum Using EEG with Mental and Temporal Effort.
authors: Bernadete Márcia Voichcoski Franco da Rosa
papers.summary: In 25 clinically stable schizophrenia patients and 11 healthy controls, EEG combined with a timed mental effort task showed that after effort, schizophrenia patients had 7.89% lower Vtotal and 16.35% lower frequency parameter, and only 6.1% of patients sustained full effort duration versus 57.9% of controls.

papers.title: A unified fixed-wavelet transformer decodes eight EEG classes across motor imagery, P300, and SSVEP paradigms.
papers.summary: The authors developed a unified fixed-wavelet Transformer (Analformer) that decoded eight EEG classes across motor imagery, P300, and SSVEP paradigms in 54 participants, achieving 71.00% mean accuracy after participant-specific fine-tuning, outperforming EEG-Conformer (54.53%), EEGNet (52.30%), and ShallowConvNet (45.35%), with ablation analyses confirming the contributions of fixed wavelets and two-stage training.

papers.title: Lesion-directed quantitative EEG after reperfusion therapy is associated with malignant cerebral edema and functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke: a prospective exploratory cohort study.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 49 acute ischemic stroke patients, a lesion-directed alpha-to-delta ratio (lesion-ADR) from a 7-min EEG within 72 h after reperfusion was associated with malignant cerebral edema (AUC 0.888 for lesion-ADR + ΔT) and functional outcomes, with associations attenuated for 90-day outcome after adjusting for admission NIHSS.

papers.title: Systematic review of machine and deep learning in EEG Alzheimer's detection.
authors: Vuddagiri Mutya Naga Sri Surya Venkata Krishna Rao Gupta
papers.summary: This systematic literature review surveyed existing primary studies applying machine learning and deep learning to EEG for Alzheimer's disease detection, focusing on preprocessing, feature extraction, and classification, and assessed algorithm performance and deployment challenges.

papers.title: Single-cell dataset of juvenile mouse neurons from the thalamic reticular nucleus: whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology.
papers.summary: The authors release a single-cell whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology dataset from 19 thalamic reticular nucleus interneurons of juvenile (P24–P34) C57Bl/6J mice, covering passive membrane properties, action potential waveform, firing patterns, and rebound-burst dynamics. The resource comprises 18,015 sweeps in NWB format with Parquet indexing and FAIR metadata for computational modeling and machine learning.

papers.title: The Effects of Methylphenidate on the EEG of Children with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder.
papers.summary: This study compared eyes-closed resting EEG in 50 children with ADHD and 50 typically developing children, recording a second EEG 1.5 h after 10 mg methylphenidate in the clinical group. Unmedicated ADHD children showed elevated delta and posterior theta and reduced alpha and gamma activity; methylphenidate increased global absolute and relative beta and relative gamma, though the authors question whether this represents normalization.

papers.title: Under-recognized Autoimmune Encephalitis in Patients with Alzheimer's Disease: A Case Series Emphasizing EEG Screening.
papers.summary: A case series of two biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer's disease patients with comorbid autoimmune encephalitis (anti-LGI1 and probable seronegative) reports rapid cognitive decline and argues that routine EEG screening can trigger autoimmune evaluation; immunotherapy and anti-amyloid treatment were associated with cognitive improvement on the MMSE.

papers.title: The association between depressive symptoms, physical activity, flow state, and resting-state EEG in college students.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 216 college students, physical exercise was associated with fewer depressive symptoms and greater flow proneness, and frontal EEG lateralization differed by depressive symptoms, but EEG-related indirect effects in serial mediation models became non-significant after adjustment for sex and self-rated physical health, whereas the flow-related indirect effect remained significant.

papers.title: Interrupted-Sampling Repeater Jamming Suppression for Frequency-Agile Radar Based on Time-Frequency Analysis and Multi-Domain Filtering.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a joint time-frequency analysis and multi-domain filtering method to suppress interrupted-sampling repeater jamming in frequency-agile radar, using STFT-based two-dimensional feature extraction and adaptive notch filtering; simulations showed suppression of coherent false targets with higher peak signal-to-jamming-plus-noise ratios than a reference method across tested SNR and JSR ranges.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
